title: HFrEF: starting and titrating guideline-directed therapy

source.citation: Gauer RL, Rifaat A, Foulkrod AM. Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: Medical Management. Am Fam Physician. 2025;112(2):131-145.

questions.q: By about how much does the combination of all four GDMT classes reduce all-cause mortality compared with placebo?
questions.why: For a 50-year-old that works out to about 7.9 extra years of life, from a network meta-analysis of the individual trials.

questions.q: Within what window after diagnosis should GDMT be titrated to target doses?
questions.why: Reaching targets within 6 weeks lowers 180-day mortality or readmission, but a 12-week schedule is acceptable (SORT A).

questions.q: A patient on lisinopril is being switched to sacubitril-valsartan. What must happen first?
questions.a: A 36-hour washout after the last ACE inhibitor dose
d: Nothing; start it the next day
A week at half the lisinopril dose
questions.why: The washout prevents angioedema. Switching from an ARB needs no washout at all.

questions.q: Which is the preferred first-line renin-angiotensin agent in HFrEF?
questions.why: Against enalapril it cut cardiovascular death with an NNT of 32 and heart failure readmissions by 21% over 27 months.

questions.q: When is sacubitril-valsartan best tolerated at initiation?
questions.a: While the patient is still congested, often during an admission
d: Only after beta blockers reach target
questions.why: Patients who cannot tolerate any agent in this class because of adverse effects or hyperkalemia are started on isosorbide dinitrate and hydralazine instead.

questions.q: Which beta blockers have proven mortality benefit in HFrEF?
questions.why: Benefit is dose dependent, so titration continues toward target even through transient worsening of symptoms.

questions.q: A patient on long-term carvedilol is admitted with decompensated heart failure. What should happen to the beta blocker?
questions.why: If a beta blocker is held during an admission, it is restarted at discharge; leaving it off raises death and readmission rates.

questions.q: When should a beta blocker be started in newly diagnosed HFrEF?
questions.a: Once the patient has been adequately diuresed
d: Only after ejection fraction is rechecked
Only if heart rate is above 100
questions.why: In new-onset heart failure with NYHA class IV symptoms it is withheld until the patient is stabilised.

questions.q: Why might eplerenone be chosen over spironolactone?
questions.a: Fewer endocrine adverse effects such as gynecomastia
d: Safe at any level of kidney function
questions.why: Both cut mortality by 15% to 30% and hospitalisation by 15% to 40%; the difference is receptor selectivity, not efficacy.

questions.q: In which HFrEF patients do SGLT-2 inhibitors reduce morbidity and mortality?
questions.a: All patients, regardless of diabetes status
d: Only patients with an eGFR above 60
Only patients not taking a diuretic
questions.why: Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin each cut their primary outcome by about a quarter on top of optimal therapy (SORT A).

questions.q: What is the NNT for empagliflozin to prevent one cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalisation?
questions.why: Dapagliflozin's NNT for death or worsening heart failure was 21. Both trials added the drug to optimal medical therapy.

questions.q: A newly diagnosed patient has a systolic blood pressure of 95 mm Hg. Which classes are started first?
questions.why: They cut sudden death and readmission with little effect on blood pressure; the RAS/neprilysin inhibitor follows in 1 to 2 weeks and the mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist 1 to 2 weeks after that.

questions.q: A patient's ejection fraction has recovered from 30% to 50% on GDMT. What happens to the medications?
d: Stop them one class at a time
Stop only the mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
questions.why: Stopping GDMT after recovery leads to recurrence of symptoms and a fall in ejection fraction; this is improved ejection fraction, not cure.

questions.q: A patient on sacubitril-valsartan has a rising BNP. How should this be interpreted?
d: Treatment failure; switch to an ACE inhibitor
questions.why: Neprilysin inhibition raises BNP, whereas increases in NT-proBNP during treatment are rare, so NT-proBNP is the peptide that tracks response.

questions.q: How often are RAS/neprilysin inhibitors and beta blockers stepped up during titration?
questions.why: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists step up every 4 weeks, and SGLT-2 inhibitors have no titration at all.
